$comment: APR expression binding vectors. The LANGUAGE is CEL and is conformance-tested by cel-spec's own suite, which this project does not maintain. What is APR-specific, and therefore tested here, is the BINDING: how expectedDataType becomes a CEL type environment, what happens to a response that will not bind, and how a result is marshalled back to a stored string.

languageConformance.note: Borrowed, not maintained here. An implementation should pass it for the language itself.

cases.name: typed arithmetic needs no conversion wrappers
free text in a typed field does not bind, so the expression degrades
cases.note: The response is stored verbatim and stays valid. It simply does not participate.

cases.name: an empty typed field is an error, never zero
cases.note: Binding empty as 0 would make a blank field silently total as zero: a wrong answer rather than no answer.

cases.name: a string field always binds, because any string is a valid response
boolean reads the generous set and writes the canonical form
a bare string is not a condition
cases.note: CEL requires bool. This is a type error the author sees at authoring time, and which degrades at fill time.

cases.name: an undeclared reference degrades rather than throwing
short-circuit survives an unbindable operand
cases.note: CEL's short-circuiting means false && error is false. Sensible partial evaluation for free.

cases.name: a double result marshals without grouping
a bool result marshals to the canonical write form
multichoice binds as a list, newline separated
multichoice accepts the legacy comma form on read
date fields bind as timestamps and compare directly
cases.note: No timestamp() wrappers: the date hint declares the type, so the comparison is what an author means.

cases.name: an unparseable date does not bind
cases.note: A perfectly valid response that simply does not participate.

cases.name: a timestamp result marshals to RFC 3339
